acceptance: Document architectural requirements, client protocols, and ingestion models for Flink SQL, ksqlDB, Feldera, Arroyo, Timeplus, and Epsio.
Identify gaps between BenchBox's batch execution harness and the requirements of streaming benchmarks (watermarks, event generators, latency vs throughput).
Define a phased platform adapter strategy prioritizing systems with existing protocol overlap (Postgres wire or ClickHouse family).
description:
Evaluate architectural feasibility and benchmarking support for pure streaming SQL and incremental view engines:

Target systems:
- Apache Flink SQL: Industry reference streaming baseline; foundation for most managed cloud streaming services.
- ksqlDB (Confluent): Kafka-native streaming SQL engine for stream processing and materialized table state.
- Feldera (DBSP): Differential/incremental-computation engine for continuous analytics over changing data.
- Arroyo: Rust-based distributed streaming SQL engine; architectural peer to modern Rust streaming runtimes.
- Timeplus: Streaming SQL built over a ClickHouse-family core; natural extension to BenchBox's existing ClickHouse support.
- Epsio: Incremental materialized view engine presenting a PostgreSQL-compatible wire protocol.

Evaluation scope & design challenges:
- Benchmark workload model: BenchBox's current harness is batch-oriented (generate -> load -> timed query loop). Streaming engines require sustained streaming event generators, event-time watermarks, windowed aggregations, stateful streaming joins, and event-to-sink latency measurements.
- Source/sink infrastructure: Source integration requirements (Kafka/Redpanda topics, CDC streams, HTTP ingestion) and containerized local UAT harnesses.
- Wire protocol / client SDK matrix: PostgreSQL wire protocol (Epsio, Timeplus PG endpoint) vs SQL REST APIs (Flink Gateway, ksqlDB REST, Arroyo API) vs native Python clients.
